Subject: Region hosting attestation + private connectivity diagram request

Hi Priya,

Thanks for taking this on. As part of our procurement and security intake we need a short attestation confirming Redwood's production hosting for our tenant will be limited to US regions only (no cross-border failover), and a PrivateLink/Privatelink-style diagram showing VPC peering or private endpoint flows. Our InfoSec team specifically asked for evidence that: 1) node scheduling for our tenant is restricted to the US region(s) we select, 2) KMS keys used for tenant encryption are region-scoped and never exported, and 3) there is an ops contact list for on-call/incident escalation during peering setup.

Could you send a simple PDF we can put into our vendor risk portal (SOC2/SIG friendly) and a diagram showing the PrivateLink connectivity options (NAT/Egress behavior, peering endpoints, and expected IP ranges)? If you can also list the slices of the CAIQ/SIG where this is addressed that would speed review.

We're hoping to close this by next Tuesday (2025-06-24). Let me know if that's feasible.

Best,
Claire

Claire/Priya — attaching the diagram and ops contact list as discussed. Summary of technical points (short, for your portal):

- Node placement: Customers may request region pinning at provisioning. For MediSys we will schedule inference workloads onto dedicated tenancy within the requested region(s) (us-west-2 or us-east-1). Automatic cross-region failover is disabled by default; failover only occurs via a manual runbook-based escalation.
- KMS/HSM: Tenant data-at-rest keys are managed with customer-scoped CMKs when requested. Keys are created in the selected region and are not exported. We use HSM-backed key wrapping for root-of-trust; key material does not leave the AWS region where it was generated.
- Private connectivity: Two supported patterns — (A) AWS PrivateLink endpoint (recommended) where traffic terminates at a regional NLB within the selected region and (B) VPC Peering + NAT gateway for customers who need direct VPC routes. Diagram shows both flows, expected ports 443 (TLS) and 8443 (control plane), recommended CIDR overlay and expected ephemeral IP ranges for peering.
- Egress: Application-level egress occurs from the same region (no forced cross-border egress). If you enable third-party integrations that route externally we can document those flows per integration.
- Audit evidence: We reference SOC2 report Section 3.2 (Access controls), SIG mapping ID SIG-PIVOT-21 (key management), and CAIQ control e.g., IAM-2, CR-3 for network segregation. Rishi included exact artifact ids below.

Attachments included: privatelink-diagram-v1.pdf (diagram, redacted IPs), ops-contacts.csv (on-call + escalation matrix), redwood-region-assertion.pdf (signed draft).

Marissa Cole
Network & Platform Solutions

Thanks everyone — I received the PDF and diagram and those look good. A couple of quick clarifying items for our InfoSec reviewer before I close the ticket:

1) Can you confirm the KMS statement for the attestation PDF to explicitly say "KMS keys created for MediSys tenant will be region-scoped and key material will never be exported outside the region's HSM"? The current draft is good but our legal wants that phrase verbatim.
2) For the PrivateLink flow — can you confirm whether the TLS termination happens at the NLB or is passed-through to the service? We need to know whether client cert mutual TLS is possible through the path.

If you can reply to those two points in-line I'll attach and close. Thanks for the quick turnaround — appreciate the ops contact CSV; I'll ping the on-call once we pick a peer window.

Claire
